prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding the homeland of a people in the Psalm 83 confederacy against Israel
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding the homeland of a people in the confederacy against Israel in Psalm 83:6-11 (Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines, Tyre, Assur), or a people or place the psalm recalls from earlier victories (Midian, the brook Kison, En-dor)
prompts.note: Philistine Gaza is in Palestine; Philistine Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath are in Israel, so both count.
prompts.summary: Psalm 83, a psalm of Asaph, describes nations that took crafty counsel to cut Israel off: Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines and Tyre, helped by Assur. The psalmist asks the Lord to deal with them as with Midian and with Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kison (Ps 83).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and Ammon are in the confederacy (Ps 83:6-7).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Assur also is joined with them (Ps 83:8).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The psalm recalls Sisera and Jabin at the brook of Kison, who perished at En-dor (Ps 83:9-10).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The inhabitants of Tyre join the confederacy (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The Philistines are in the confederacy; their city Gaza is in the Gaza Strip (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: The psalm recalls the Midianites (Ps 83:9); Church Bible Map 9 plots Midian east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose very first stake (a group of congregations) was organized 1995-1997 (Northern Ireland counts as UK)
prompts.text_original: In just three years, 1995 to 1997, the Church organized first stakes in countries as far apart as Ireland, Thailand, Kiribati and Haiti. A country whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1995 and 1997.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Ireland, Singapore, Thailand, Papua New Guinea, Kiribati, DR Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Haiti)
prompts.note: Ireland counts: Dublin's 1995 stake was its first. Belfast's 1974 stake is in the United Kingdom.
prompts.summary: In 1995 the Church organized first stakes in Singapore, Dublin, Bangkok and Port Moresby. Kiribati and Zaire, now DR Congo, followed in 1996, and Cote d'Ivoire and Haiti in 1997, showing how quickly the Church was maturing in Asia, the Pacific, Africa and the Caribbean.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: The Dublin Ireland Stake, the first in the Republic of Ireland, was organized March 12, 1995.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: The Zaire Kinshasa Stake, the first in the country, was organized November 3, 1996.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: The Port-au-Prince Haiti Stake, the first in Haiti, was organized September 21, 1997.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: The Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Stake was created October 22, 1995, with Vaiba Rome as president.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: The Singapore Stake was organized February 26, 1995, with Leonard Woo as president.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Elder Neal A. Maxwell created the Bangkok Thailand Stake, June 18-19, 1995.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: The Abidjan Cote d'Ivoire Stake, the country's first, was organized August 17, 1997.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Elder L. Tom Perry organized the Tarawa Kiribati Stake, August 11, 1996.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology names a woman who translated the Book of Mormon
prompts.text_original: A country or territory whose Global Histories chronology names a woman as a translator of the Book of Mormon, in whole or in part, into a local language
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Albania, Thailand, Ghana, Bulgaria, Iceland, Guam, Zimbabwe
prompts.note: Scoped to the Global Histories chronologies read 27 Oct 2026; women have translated scripture in many other languages too.
prompts.summary: Local members, many of them women, have carried much of the work of translating the Book of Mormon. Church chronologies name Evangeline Coy for Bulgarian, Srilaksana Suntarahut for Thai, Sveinbjorg Gudmundsdottir for Icelandic, Maria Salas Calvo for CHamoru, Priscilla Sampson-Davis for Fante and two lead translators for Albanian.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: Brikena Ribaj and Juventila Sinamati were lead translators of the Albanian edition of 1999.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Srilaksana Suntarahut joined the review committee in 1970 and was principal translator of the 1976 Thai edition.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Evangeline Kokotanova Coy, a convert in the United States, finished the first Bulgarian manuscript in 1934.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Priscilla Sampson-Davis began translating hymns into Fante in 1980 and later translated the Book of Mormon.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: Maria Salas Calvo translated the CHamoru selections issued in book form in 1989.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Sveinbjorg Gudmundsdottir and Halldor Hansen translated the Icelandic edition published in 1981.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Dorothy Tembo was on the team whose Shona triple combination, Book of Mormon included, came out in 2007.
